title: Can a Person Be Arrested Without a Court Warrant in Ethiopia?
description: I want to understand the rules in Ethiopia regarding arrest without a court warrant. In what situations can the police arrest a person without first getting a warrant from a judge? What rights does the arrested person have after being taken into custody? How quickly must the person be brought before a court, and what happens if the police keep the person longer than the law allows? Also, can evidence collected after an unlawful arrest be used in court?

title: Private Inquiry Test: Commercial lease breach in Addis
description: My landlord in Bole Addis Ababa locked the premises without court notice.

answers.content: Under Ethiopian Commercial Code and Civil Code Art 2945, lockouts without court eviction orders are unlawful.

title: Can police hold a suspect in detention for more than 48 hours without a court remand?
description: My cousin was detained by local police on Friday afternoon on suspicion of property damage. They told the family he cannot see a judge until Tuesday because of the weekend. Is this legal under Ethiopian law?

answers.content: No, this is a clear violation of constitutional rights. Under Article 19(3) of the FDRE Constitution, every arrested person MUST be brought before a court of law within 48 hours of arrest (excluding reasonable transit time). Courts operate duty judges on weekends for remand hearings (የጊዜ ቀጠሮ). You should immediately engage an advocate to file a writ of Habeas Corpus (የአካል ነፃነት አቤቱታ) demanding his immediate release or court appearance.
We had a similar situation in Kirkos sub-city last year. Once our lawyer presented the petition on Monday morning, the judge ordered the station commander to explain the detention.

title: What happens to common property in divorce if the house was built on leased land?
description: My husband and I are separating after 8 years of marriage. We built a G+1 house during our marriage on an urban lease plot that was registered in his name only. Am I entitled to half the house value?

answers.content: Yes, absolutely. Under Article 62 and 63 of the Revised Family Code (Proclamation No. 213/2000), any building or immovable improvement constructed during the subsistence of marriage is legally presumed to be common marital property (የጋራ ንብረት), regardless of whose name appears on the municipal lease title deed. The court will order an independent certified engineering valuation, and you will be awarded 50% of the net equity or an order for public auction division.

Make sure you immediately file for an injunction order (የእግድ ትእዛዝ) at the Federal First Instance or High Court to prevent any unauthorized sale, transfer, or bank mortgage on the property while the divorce is pending.

title: Can a One-Person Company (OPC) have foreign investment under the 2021 Commercial Code?
description: I am a foreign investor exploring opening a tech consultancy in Addis Ababa. Can I register a One-Person Company (OPC) without local Ethiopian nominee partners?

answers.content: Yes, under the revised Commercial Code of Ethiopia (Proclamation No. 1243/2021, Article 534), a single shareholder can form an OPC with limited liability. However, as a foreign national, your entity must also comply with the Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020 minimum capital requirements (typically $200,000 USD for 100% foreign ownership, or $150,000 USD if in joint venture with a domestic investor).

title: My employer terminated my contract after 70 days without written notice. What can I claim?
description: I was hired as a senior accountant on probation. After 70 calendar days, the manager verbally told me not to come back on Monday. They refuse to pay my final month salary.

answers.content: Under Article 11 of Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, the maximum probation period in Ethiopia is strictly 60 working days. Because you worked past 60 days without written termination, you automatically attained permanent employee status. A verbal dismissal without written notice and lawful grounds is an unlawful termination (ያለአግባብ ስንብት). You are legally entitled to: 1) Full unpaid wages; 2) Severance pay; 3) Compensation for unlawful dismissal equal to up to 3 months' salary.
